CR: complete resection group; IR: incomplete resection group.
CR : exérèse complète ; IR : exérèse incomplete.
Adjuvant systemic therapy was given to patients with axil-
lary lymph node involvement and consisted of chemotherapy for
premenopausal and Tamoxifen
for postmenopausal patients.
Radiotherapy had to start within nine weeks after lumpectomy
for patients not given adjuvant chemotherapy. A total dose of
50 Gy of whole breast irradiation was delivered with two tan-
gential megavoltage photon beams over a 5-week period, with a
dose of 2 Gy per fraction, in agreement with ICRU report 50 [9].
The boost dose was specified at point B, located at the centre of
the lumpectomy area. The boost dose had to be delivered with
a direct electron beam or with tangential photon fields given in
fractions of 2 Gy, or with an iridium 192 implant at a dose rate
of 0,5 Gy per hour.
All analyses were carried out according to the intent-to-
treat policy. The randomization was performed centrally at the
EORTC Data Centre using the minimisation technique [10].
Time to any event was calculated from the date of randomisation.
Data for patients, who remained free of an event were censored
at the date of last visit. Survival was compared by Logrank test,
local control and fibrosis rates by Gray test, all at the 2-sided
significance level of 0.01 for the CR group and at 0.05 for the
IR group [8].
3. Results
3.1. Patient, tumour and radiotherapy characteristics
A total of 5569 early stage breast cancer patients underwent
a lumpectomy followed by whole breast irradiation of 50 Gy.
Five thousand three hundred and eighteen patients in whom
the lumpectomy was microscopically complete according to
the local pathologist were randomised between a boost dose of
16 Gy (2661 patients) and no boost dose (2657 patients) and 251
patients after an incomplete lumpectomy received either a boost
dose of 10 Gy (126 patients) or 26 Gy (125 Gy). The median
follow-up was 10.8 years. Characteristics of the patients were
similar within both the complete and the incomplete resection
groups but showed differences between these groups (Table 1):
patients in the incomplete resection group had a higher tumour
stage with 28% versus 20% stage T2 and 35% versus 21%
involved lymph nodes. A re-excision was performed more often
in the complete resection group (25% versus 14%). There were
no marked differences in the characteristics of whole breast irra-
diation between the four groups (Table 2). An interstitial boost
was more often used in the patients randomised to a high boost
dose after an IR (28% of boost treatments versus 9% for the CR
group and 10% for the low boost dose IR, respectively).
3.2. Local control
For patients with a complete tumour resection, the cumula-
tive incidence of local recurrence at 10 years was 10.2% (95%
CI: 8.7–11.8%) without a boost and 6.2% (95% CI: 4.9–7.5%)
with a boost (p < 0.0001). The hazard ratio for local recurrence
was 0.59 (99% CI: 0.46–0.76) after a boost. The absolute risk
for local recurrence was strongly correlated with the age of the
patient. Therefore, notwithstanding the absence of a statistically
significant interaction between the magnitude of the relative risk
